title: Unpatterned Wafer Inspection - Pattern Defects Detection on WaferSight PWG
subtitle: Final Inspection Quality Validation for 45nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Yuki Tanaka

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the WaferSight PWG system to detect and classify Pattern Defects defects during final inspection inspection at the 45nm technology node. The test is conducted at Hsinchu Fab 15 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Pattern Defects defects that are critical to yield at the 45nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the WaferSight PWG platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: WaferSight PWG
- Inspection Type: Unpatterned Wafer Inspection
- Target Defect: Pattern Defects
- Process Step: Final Inspection
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 45nm
- Fab Location: Hsinchu Fab 15

This test case applies to all WaferSight PWG systems deployed at Hsinchu Fab 15 for final inspection monitoring in the 45nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: WaferSight PWG
Software Version: v13.2.144
Recipe: UNPATTERNED_WAFER_INSPECTION_45nm_FINAL INSPECTION
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Medium (157 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.1μm
Edge Exclusion: 3mm
Sampling Plan: 21-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the WaferSight PWG system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Unpatterned Wafer Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Pattern Defects defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 45nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 107 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 97% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.1% for Unpatterned Wafer Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.98 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-10-08
Wafers Tested: 16
Total Defects Found: 4668
Defect Density: 1485.87 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 3.2%
Capture Rate: 99.0%
Test Duration: 204 minutes
System Uptime: 97.1%

Result Classification: PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The WaferSight PWG demonstrated excellent performance in detecting Pattern Defects at the 45nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Cross-correlation with the reference SEM confirmed classification accuracy.

e) Recipe portability between systems at this fab was confirmed.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS: No corrective actions required. Test passed all acceptance criteria.
